theory.intro: Parallel-line problems usually need a chain: move an angle across the parallel lines with a parallel-line property, then use a relationship at one point.
facts: Corresponding and alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.
Co-interior angles on parallel lines add to $180^{\circ}$.
Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$, angles at a point add to $360^{\circ}$, and vertically opposite angles are equal.
Write a reason at every step so the chain can be checked.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so $a=64^{\circ}$.
Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}x+64^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\x&=180^{\circ}-64^{\circ}\\x&=116^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $a=57^{\circ}$.
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal, so $x=a=57^{\circ}$.

Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so $a=112^{\circ}$.
Co-interior angles between parallel lines add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}x+112^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\x&=180^{\circ}-112^{\circ}\\x&=68^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
